-        # side branch + PR + squash auto-merge: quality.yml's crap check
-        # satisfies the ruleset, auto-merge lands it unattended. The squash
-        # subject carries [skip ci] so the merge push does not re-trigger a
-        # release (paths-ignore does not cover versions.json).
+        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
+        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
+        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
+        # cover versions.json).
+        #
+        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
+        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
+        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
+        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
+        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
+        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
+        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
+        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
+        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
+        # publishing.
         if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true

@@ -136,20 +164,43 @@ jobs:

+          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
+          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
+          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
+          git fetch origin main
+          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
+            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
+            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
+            exit 0
+          fi
           BR="chore/pack-versions/$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
           git push origin "HEAD:${BR}"
           PR_URL="$(gh pr create --head "${BR}" --title "chore(release): bump agent versions" \
             --body "Auto-generated by the pack release. Packs are already published; this lands the bumped versions.json on main so the NEXT release computes versions from the right base." 2>&1 | tail -1)"

+          # (a strict ruleset rejects it and the PR is left for the machine
+          # loop — never fail the release AFTER publishing).
+          checks_ok=false

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

/**
 * Unit tests: the pack-release pipeline (ci/release_packs.mjs +

content.text:
# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
            exit 0
          fi
          BR="chore/pack-versions/$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          git push origin "HEAD:${BR}"
          PR_URL="$(gh pr create --head "${BR}" --title "chore(release): bump agent versions" \
            --body "Auto-generated by the pack release. Packs are already published; this lands the bumped versions.json on main so the NEXT release computes versions from the right base." 2>&1 | tail -1)"
          PR_NUM="${PR_URL##*/}"
          echo "versions PR: #${PR_NUM} (${PR_URL})"
          # Wait for the required checks, then re-run the nothing-changed
          # guard BEFORE merging (guard 2 — the #689 window). --watch exits
          # non-zero on red checks or when none are reported yet; retry the
          # not-reported-yet case, then fall through to the merge attempt
          # (a strict ruleset rejects it and the PR is left for the machine
          # loop — never fail the release AFTER publishing).
          checks_ok=false
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh pr checks "${PR_NUM}" --watch --interval 15; then checks_ok=true; break; fi
            sleep 30
          done
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            gh pr close "${PR_NUM}" --comment "main already carries these agent versions (empty diff — a concurrent release landed the same ledger bump). Closing instead of merging (gh-690)." \
              || echo "::warning::could not close version PR #${PR_NUM} — leaving it for the machine loop"
            git push origin --delete "${BR}" || true
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
            exit 0
          fi
          [ "${checks_ok}" = "true" ] || echo "::warning::checks not green on version PR #${PR_NUM} — attempting merge anyway"
          gh pr merge "${PR_NUM}" --squash \
            --subject "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci] (#${PR_NUM})" \
            || echo "::warning::version PR #${PR_NUM} left open — merge via the machine loop"
          git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"

      - name: Publish the GitHub Release
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```

target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). # Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. blocks.text:
# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"

          # files make later operations refuse).

          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0

Now I have the full workflow. Let me examine potential issues:

1. **Guard 1 placement**: Guard 1 runs AFTER `git commit`. So even when main already carries the target versions, a local commit was made. But that's fine — the workflow exits and the commit is discarded (no push). OK.

2. **Guard 1 diff check**: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` — compares local HEAD versions.json vs origin/main's. If identical, skip. Good.

3. **Guard 2 placement**: after `gh pr checks --watch` loop. Re-fetches main and re-checks. If versions.json now matches main (i.e., a concurrent release landed the same bump), close the PR. Good.

4. **Potential issue with guard 2**: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` compares the LOCAL HEAD commit's versions.json with origin/main. But wait — after `git fetch origin main`, origin/main ref is updated. HEAD is still the local commit with the bump. If main's versions.json equals HEAD's versions.json, then the PR diff is empty → close. Correct.

5. **Issue — the `--watch` retry loop**: `gh pr checks "${PR_NUM}" --watch` exits non-zero "when none are reported yet" — the comment says retry. The loop retries 3 times with 30s sleeps. But if checks legitimately fail (red), it will retry 3 times then proceed to attempt the merge anyway with a warning. Then `gh pr merge` will fail because ruleset requires checks... and it degrades to a warning, leaving the PR open for the machine loop. Hmm, but that means red checks → the release is still published (packs already published in a later step — wait, actually the publish step happens after this step regardless). Actually the packs are published in the "Publish the GitHub Release" step which runs if released == 'true'. So the release is published regardless of the ledger PR merge status. This is by design ("never fail the release AFTER publishing").

6. **Issue — merge attempt after checks not green**: The comment says "a strict ruleset rejects it and the PR is left for the machine loop". OK.

7. **Potential correctness issue in Guard 2**: When guard 2 closes the PR and deletes the branch — but wait, the `gh pr close` failure path: `gh pr close ... || echo "::warning::..."`. If close fails (e.g., PR already merged), then it still does `git push origin --delete "${BR}" || true` and exits 0. OK.

8. **Timing race between guard 2 and merge**: There's still a tiny race — after guard 2 passes (diff non-empty), main could receive another identical ledger PR, and then `gh pr merge` would merge an empty-diff PR. GitHub's `gh pr merge` of a PR whose diff is empty: GitHub will still merge it (creates an empty merge commit or refuses?). Actually in the gh-690 incident, #689 merged with a 0-byte diff — so GitHub does allow merging an empty-diff PR. The residual race window is small (between the last fetch and the merge), but the guard narrows it dramatically. This is inherent TOCTOU; acceptable, worth a suggestion note maybe.

9. **The `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json`** — one subtlety: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` — diff between HEAD and origin/main restricted to versions.json. But if origin/main has MOVED FORWARD with different content (e.g., another ledger with HIGHER versions), then the diff is non-empty and the workflow proceeds to merge its own PR → merge conflict? Actually a squash merge of the PR branch (which is based on older main) — GitHub will attempt merge; if conflict in versions.json, it fails → warning → left for machine loop. OK as designed.

10. **A subtle issue**: Guard 2 compares HEAD vs origin/main — but what if main moved with a DIFFERENT ledger (e.g., #688 landed with sm_github 0.1.24 while this run bumped sm_github to 0.1.24 as well — identical). Then diff is quiet → close. Good. If main moved with a different ledger (versions differ), diff non-empty → merge attempt → conflict → machine loop. Good.

11. **`for attempt in 1 2 3`** — the variable `attempt` is unused (shellcheck SC2034 would flag). Minor nit.

12. **`--watch --interval 15`** — polling interval 15s; the checks could take minutes; total wait unbounded? `gh pr checks --watch` waits until all checks complete — could be a long wait, but that's intended. If checks take very long... unbounded wait in CI. Hmm, no timeout on --watch. The job-level default timeout is 360 min. Probably fine.

13. **The sync step (`git reset --hard origin/main`)**: Gated to push events. But note the ordering: "Compute base ref (last release tag)" runs BEFORE the sync — the base tag computation uses git tags which are unaffected by the reset (tags are fetched by checkout with fetch-depth: 0). Fine.

However — there's a subtle problem: `git reset --hard origin/main` on a push event. The push event's checkout SHA IS a main commit (push to main). The reset to origin/main moves HEAD to the latest main — which may include commits pushed AFTER the trigger SHA. That's the intended fix.

But wait — a potential issue: if the run was triggered by a push to main, and then reset to origin/main, then the step "Bump versions.json via PR" commits on top of origin/main — good.

14. **`dist/.no-release` logic**: In release_packs.mjs — the build writes `dist/.no-release` when nothing to release. Let me check release_packs.mjs fully to verify the no-release path exists and how the affected set is computed after the reset. Let me read the full file.

15. **Phantom versions agent fix**: `allAgents()` now uses `agentNamesFromFiles`. And `computeAffectedSet` skips the ledger file. Also the ledger `versions.json` no longer has the "versions" key. Good.

But — hmm, one question: does `computeAffectedSet` also have the `!file.startsWith('package')` inline check that duplicates the guard's classification? Yes:

```js
if (file.endsWith('.json') && !file.includes('/') && !file.startsWith('package')) {
  affected.add(basename(file, '.json')); // a root entry config changed
}
```

This duplicates `isAgentConfigFile` logic inline instead of reusing `isAgentConfigFile`. That's a DRY violation — the classification now lives in two places (the guard module and the inline check in computeAffectedSet). # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.
