blocks.text:
# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). # Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.

        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")

          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.

        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). blocks.text:
# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-690 fix design is sound (sync-to-`origin/main` for queued runs, dual nothing-changed guards replacing `--auto`, phantom-ledger cleanup, 21 new tests), but the new guard module misclassifies any 4-char root entry (`.git`, `.fah`, `docs`, `site`) as an agent — the next release will crash building `.fa.json` and, if it survived, would re-import the exact phantom-agent class this PR removes.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING: broken `.json` suffix check in `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs:33` (`-1 !== -1` passes for names < 5 chars) → phantom agents `.fa`/`.gi`/`doc`/`sit` on every release (details + ES5-safe fix inline)
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `computeAffectedSet()` still re-implements agent classification inline instead of routing through the new guard module
- 💡 3 suggestions: workflow retry-loop nits, a weak close-failure test assertion, and a factually wrong "REAL secret" claim in the committed memory note

Verified along the way: ticket ACs are met (close-not-merge guards ✓, concurrency group confirmed and pinned by a test ✓, ledger audit explains the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 skew as the stale-ledger race ✓); the `origin_url` line's `${PUSH_TOKEN}` is shell interpolation of a workflow secret, not a committed credential; the guard-2 → `gh pr merge` window keeps a small (seconds) TOCTOU that is inherent to the design and acceptable.

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix the suffix check (`file.slice(-'.json'.length) !== '.json'`), add the root-shaped regression cases to `test_releasePacks.js`, then re-verify `node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run` lists no `.fa`/`.gi`/`doc`/`sit`
2. Route `computeAffectedSet()` through `isAgentConfigFile`/`toAgentName`
3. Optional polish per the inline suggestions

### Thread 7

The rework leg owns open threads: agent:rework is armed on this PR and the rework runner will work through the threads and push. Validation re-runs automatically afterwards, and once the threads are resolved a fresh re-review is armed (review-threads-resolved).

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the `.json` suffix check classifies any 4-char root entry as an agent — the next release will crash, and the phantom-agent bug this PR fixes comes straight back**

`isAgentConfigFile` rejects non-`.json` names with:

```js
if (file.lastIndexOf('.json') !== file.length - '.json'.length) return false;
```

For any name shorter than 5 chars, `lastIndexOf('.json')` is **-1** and `file.length - 5` is also **-1** → `-1 !== -1` is false → the guard does **not** return false and the entry is treated as an agent. Verified against this repo's actual root listing:

| Root entry (present on the release runner) | `isAgentConfigFile` | Becomes agent |
|---|---|---|
| `.git` (created by actions/checkout) | `true` | `.gi` |
| `.fah` (tracked dir) | `true` | `.fa` |
| `docs` (tracked dir) | `true` | `doc` |
| `site` (tracked dir) | `true` | `sit` |

`allAgents()` = `agentNamesFromFiles(readdirSync(ROOT))` runs against the runner's checkout, so the next push-triggered release gets `['.fa', '.gi', … 'doc', 'sit', … real agents]` and then, in `main()`:

1. `buildPack('.fa', '0.1.0')` → `dmtools compile .fa.json …` → `.fa.json` does not exist → `execFileSync` throws → **the release job fails** (phantom names sort first, so it dies immediately).
2. If the build ever got past that, the loop sets `versions['.fa']`/`versions['.gi']`/… and `writeFileSync(VERSIONS_FILE, …)` re-pollutes the ledger this PR just cleaned, plus phantom zips in the release and catalog — the exact gh-690 phantom-agent class.

Note the PR's own verification cannot catch it: `node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run` never calls `buildPack`, so the bogus names only print harmless catalog lines.

Fix (ES5-safe, matching this module's `var`/`indexOf` style — `String.prototype.slice` with a negative index is ES3+):

```js
if (file.slice(-'.json'.length) !== '.json') return false;
```

And please add the regression cases the suite is missing — every `agentNamesFromFiles` test feeds hand-picked arrays, none uses root-shaped names, which is why this shipped:

```js
test('short non-json root entries (dirs like .git/.fah/docs/site) are not agent configs', function () {
    assert.equal(guard().isAgentConfigFile('.git'), false);
    assert.equal(guard().isAgentConfigFile('.fah'), false);
    assert.equal(guard().isAgentConfigFile('docs'), false);
    assert.equal(guard().isAgentConfigFile('site'), false);
});
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: agent classification is still duplicated inline in `computeAffectedSet()`**

The PR moves classification into the unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs` and its header claims it is "the single definition of \"what is an agent\" for discovery AND catalog building" — but the affected-set path right here keeps a second, hand-rolled copy of the same rule:

```js
if (isLedgerFile(file)) continue;
if (file.endsWith('.json') && !file.includes('/') && !file.startsWith('package')) {
  affected.add(basename(file, '.json')); // a root entry config changed
}
```

That is `isAgentConfigFile` + `toAgentName` reimplemented. The two agree today; the next person extending the classifier (say, excluding another data file the way `versions.json` just was) will fix the module, miss this copy, and a phantom agent returns through the affected-set door. Since `isAgentConfigFile` already excludes the ledger, the whole block collapses to:

```js
if (isAgentConfigFile(file)) {
  affected.add(toAgentName(file)); // a root entry config changed
}
```

One classification path also means one test surface — exactly the kind of split-brain that let the blocking suffix-check bug in `pack_release_guard.cjs:33` reach `allAgents()` while `computeAffectedSet()`'s inline `endsWith` stayed correct.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: retry-loop nits**

- `attempt` is never used (shellcheck SC2034) — `for _ in 1 2 3` or just drop the variable.
- The third failed attempt still `sleep 30`s before the loop ends. Only sleep between attempts, e.g. `[ "${attempt}" = "3" ] || sleep 30`.
- Cosmetic: this loop cannot distinguish "no checks reported yet" from genuinely red checks, so a red `crap` check burns all 3 retries (watch + ~60s) before the doomed merge attempt. That is acceptable (the ruleset rejects the merge and the warning leaves the PR for the machine loop), but a one-line comment saying red checks intentionally fall through would keep the next reader from "fixing" it.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the close-failure assertion can pass for the wrong reason**

`tail = wf.slice(close)` runs to EOF, so `tail.indexOf('::warning::') !== -1` is also satisfied by the *unrelated* merge-fallback warning (`::warning::version PR #… left open`) a few lines further down — if someone deletes the close's own `|| echo "::warning::could not close…"`, this invariant test still passes. Anchor it on the close's specific message:

```js
assert.ok(tail.indexOf('could not close version PR') !== -1,
    'a failing close must degrade to a warning, not fail the release');
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "REAL secret" claim in this note is factually wrong**

The `origin_url` line is `origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/…"` — the credential is shell-expanded from the step's `PUSH_TOKEN` env (a `secrets.*` workflow secret), not a literal token committed to the file. The `[REDACTED:Connection String Password]` in read/grep output is a scanner false positive on the `${PUSH_TOKEN}` interpolation.

Committing "contains a REAL secret" into project memory will send future sessions (and humans) hunting for a leaked PAT that does not exist…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)

        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push

        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check

        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not

        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |

          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

Now I have the full workflow. Let me examine potential issues:

1. **Guard 1 placement**: Guard 1 runs AFTER `git commit`. So even when main already carries the target versions, a local commit was made. But that's fine — the workflow exits and the commit is discarded (no push). OK.

2. **Guard 1 diff check**: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` — compares local HEAD versions.json vs origin/main's. If identical, skip. Good.

3. **Guard 2 placement**: after `gh pr checks --watch` loop. Re-fetches main and re-checks. If versions.json now matches main (i.e., a concurrent release landed the same bump), close the PR. Good.

4. **Potential issue with guard 2**: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` compares the LOCAL HEAD commit's versions.json with origin/main. But wait — after `git fetch origin main`, origin/main ref is updated. HEAD is still the local commit with the bump. If main's versions.json equals HEAD's versions.json, then the PR diff is empty → close. Correct.

5. **Issue — the `--watch` retry loop**: `gh pr checks "${PR_NUM}" --watch` exits non-zero "when none are reported yet" — the comment says retry. The loop retries 3 times with 30s sleeps. But if checks legitimately fail (red), it will retry 3 times then proceed to attempt the merge anyway with a warning. Then `gh pr merge` will fail because ruleset requires checks... and it degrades to a warning, leaving the PR open for the machine loop. Hmm, but that means red checks → the release is still published (packs already published in a later step — wait, actually the publish step happens after this step regardless). Actually the packs are published in the "Publish the GitHub Release" step which runs if released == 'true'. So the release is published regardless of the ledger PR merge status. This is by design ("never fail the release AFTER publishing").

6. **Issue — merge attempt after checks not green**: The comment says "a strict ruleset rejects it and the PR is left for the machine loop". OK.

7. **Potential correctness issue in Guard 2**: When guard 2 closes the PR and deletes the branch — but wait, the `gh pr close` failure path: `gh pr close ... || echo "::warning::..."`. If close fails (e.g., PR already merged), then it still does `git push origin --delete "${BR}" || true` and exits 0. OK.

8. **Timing race between guard 2 and merge**: There's still a tiny race — after guard 2 passes (diff non-empty), main could receive another identical ledger PR, and then `gh pr merge` would merge an empty-diff PR. GitHub's `gh pr merge` of a PR whose diff is empty: GitHub will still merge it (creates an empty merge commit or refuses?). Actually in the gh-690 incident, #689 merged with a 0-byte diff — so GitHub does allow merging an empty-diff PR. The residual race window is small (between the last fetch and the merge), but the guard narrows it dramatically. This is inherent TOCTOU; acceptable, worth a suggestion note maybe.

9. **The `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json`** — one subtlety: `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` — diff between HEAD and origin/main restricted to versions.json. But if origin/main has MOVED FORWARD with different content (e.g., another ledger with HIGHER versions), then the diff is non-empty and the workflow proceeds to merge its own PR → merge conflict? Actually a squash merge of the PR branch (which is based on older main) — GitHub will attempt merge; if conflict in versions.json, it fails → warning → left for machine loop. OK as designed.

10. **A subtle issue**: Guard 2 compares HEAD vs origin/main — but what if main moved with a DIFFERENT ledger (e.g., #688 landed with sm_github 0.1.24 while this run bumped sm_github to 0.1.24 as well — identical). Then diff is quiet → close. Good. If main moved with a different ledger (versions differ), diff non-empty → merge attempt → conflict → machine loop. Good.

If checks take very long... unbounded wait in CI. Hmm, no timeout on --watch. The job-level default timeout is 360 min. Probably fine.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 691 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/691 - **Title**: gh-690 pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23 - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-690` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +403 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:10:07Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:10:33Z ## PR Description ### What changed Hardened the pack-release pipeline against the gh-690 incident: a ledger bump PR whose target versions are already on `main` is now **closed instead of merged** (or never created), and release runs queued behind another now reset to current `main` before computing the affected set. Also removed the phantom `"versions"` agent from the release builder and the version ledger. ### Key decisions - **Nothing-changed guard, twice** (`agent-pack-release.yml`): skip PR creation when `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` is empty; re-run the same check after `gh pr checks --watch` and `gh pr close` when main caught up mid-flight. Replaced `gh pr merge --auto` — it merges server-side the moment checks pass and cannot re-verify the diff (exactly how #689 merged with a 0-byte diff). - **Queued runs release current main**: new sync step (`git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, push events only) after checkout — a queued run previously computed bumps from its trigger SHA's stale ledger, double-bumping agents whose content landed mid-queue (the `sm_github`/`pr_review` 0.1.24 off-by-one). A run that finds everything released writes `dist/.no-release` and no-ops. - **Ledger audit result**: `allAgents()` swept root `*.json` — including `versions.json` itself — into a phantom `versions` agent (bogus ledger key + a `versions-*.zip` in every release). Classification now lives in the pure, unit-tested `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`; the phantom key is deleted from `versions.json`. The double bump of `sm_github`/`pr_review` to 0.1.24 is the stale-ledger race above, not lost content — the next release recomputes from the corrected ledger. - Concurrency group `agent-pack-release` (cancel-in-progress: false) verified present — runs serialize; the race was the stale checkout, not a missing group. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json # new suite, 21 tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite, 1414 passed node ci/release_packs.mjs --dry-run # no phantom "versions" agent ```
Guard flow ```mermaid flowchart TD B[Build + validate packs] --> C[Commit versions.json] C --> G1{main already carries
target versions?} G1 -->|yes| S[Skip PR — ::notice] G1 -->|no| P[Push branch + create PR] P --> W[gh pr checks --watch] W --> G2{main already carries
target versions?} G2 -->|yes| X[gh pr close + delete branch] G2 -->|no| M[Squash merge \[skip ci\]] ```

# gh-690: pack-release: empty bump PRs merge when content lands mid-flight (no nothing-changed guard) + sm_github version skew 0.1.24 vs 0.1.23

## Description

Live 2026-10-04 05:40-05:48: three content PRs (#684/#685/#686) merged within 3 min → release automation produced THREE bump PRs (#687/#688/#689) and **#689 merged with a 0-byte diff** (its branch was cut before #688 landed; merge message literally shows 'Merge branch main into chore/pack-versions/20261004-054742'). An empty PR rode the full review/merge cycle.

Fix: when the bump branch finds main already carries the target versions (empty diff), CLOSE the PR instead of merging (or skip creating it). Also check the double-trigger: one content merge batch produced overlapping bump runs (concurrency group missing?).

Secondary: latest release agents-rel-20261004-054747 ships sm_github-0.1.24.zip while every other agent is 0.1.23 — one extra bump for sm_github; audit the version ledger for the off-by-one.
